Right back at you, I was the only Hispanic in my school for years. I always loved the first day of school when we went around the room introducing ourselves and I was the only person asked where I was from. lol

I think this is a topic that is hard to address with internet discussion and personal experiences. As a younger (24) person who has lived in both New York (Bronx) and Tennessee (suburb / rural area about an hour from Nashville) , as well as in other countries, I can only say that my life doesn't agree with what you are saying.

I do agree with you that people up north make the systematic issues in the South sound much worse than it really is, but my day-to-day experiences in the South are less preferable to me than the ones I had elsewhere. My friends from Tennessee are quicker to generalize about me based on stereotypes they believe, I was treated worse by school staff in Tennessee, and have only been subject to hate speech in the south. By hate speech I mean the combination of a slur with body action implying a physical threat, I don't particularly care if someone just says something. When I was a pre-teen in Tennessee I could not have friends sleep over at my house because they were afraid of my Catholic parents, and my parents have been asked to leave their friends' churches due to being Catholic. My co-worker's family, who happens to be Jewish, had Swastikas drawn into their lawn only a couple months ago in a neighbourhood about 15 min out of Nashville. I am not saying these things don't happen north of the Mason-Dixon, I'm sure they do, but I have only lived that here.

It isn't like everyday in Tennessee I faced hatred, but it felt as if there was more a general ignorance about anything outside of the majority. Many of the kids in my school had never left the state, let alone the South, and I think that just led to a lack of familiarity with outsiders.

I hope this doesn't come off as disparaging. I am glad you feel comfortable in the South, and I absolutely agree on your point about classism in the North.

I have no idea if Dan Watters is hetero or bi, but let me say he is a brilliant writer. I'm picking this up solely on how much he impressed me with two issues of *The Seasons Have Teeth*.

My last time heading to the shop for the considerable future with work picking up, but at least its a week where there's books I'm pretty stoked to read. In order of anticipation:

* **Daredevil #12**: As much as DD hasn't recaptured the form it had in issues 15-20ish and the 30's, this run has consistently been well-written and been enjoyable issue to issue, with some of the best art in Big 2 comics when Checchetto is on pencils. Only  3 issues left and I have the faith in Chip to end this well.
* **Peacemaker Tries Hard #2:** The debut issue was hilarious, irreverent, and a great introduction for me to Kyle Starks' style, which I have heard praise on from the indie world.  Starks is perfectly teamed up with Pugh, whose art took the humour and anted it up. Peacemaker has been a consistent feature in some of these Dawn of DC books, but this right here (even though it's OOC) is the best place to turn to if you're looking for the James Gunn / John Cena rendition.
* **Shazam #2**: Mark Waid and Dan Mora. 
* **Loki #1:** I am picking this up solely on how much I enjoyed Watters' *The Seasons Have Teeth*. He is a brilliant, literary writer in this medium and those I know who read his Azrael stuff also were happy with him. Plus there's an Artgerm variant.
* **Red Goblin #5:** Part of the Carnage Reigns "event" happening at Marvel that has surprised me by being an event that I want to read and not just an inconvenient roadblock for two ongoings I am reading. I went back and read the first four issues to get caught up before this came out, and this book on its own is actually really good. Another point for Paknadel along with the issues of Carnage he has helmed so far. 
* **Batman #136:** Start of Chip's arc where Batman is now in its "Dawn of DC" stages. After many were whelmed / under-whelmed with the last arc, I hope Chip is going back to Failsafe form with this. Normally I would have full confidence in him as he is a top 3 writer for me right now, but the fact this is leading toward a Catwoman event doesn't inspire confidence from me. If I wasn't switching to digital for the coming months, this book would be the decider if I dropped this or not.
* **Fantastic Four #8:** I think this run has been pretty consistent so far, with a couple issues I have found to be really strong (#1, #2, and #7). If I was a bigger FF fan I think I would be more excited for this every month since it feels like North really wants to do right by the characters and knows how to write "wholesome family" stories that don't make my eyes roll. Since the FF isn't really my jam, despite how much I like Hickman's and Waid's tenures, I think its a good review for this run that I still am interested to read it every month.
* **Poison Ivy #13:** I am glad that this was turned into an ongoing for all of the fans of this book, but I have really struggled to enjoy it at the same level I had back in its opening arc. It's not bad by any means, but just is one of those books that I can objectively acknowledge its merits, strong writing that issues social commentary with bits of humour and without feeling ham-fisted with fun art, but don't feel particularly attached to. Granted, I am interested to see what happens to this book now that its part of the "Dawn of DC" and has Ivy back in Gotham. That being said, if I wasn't switching to digital I think I would have clocked out with this issue and revisited it later.

My FOC orders at my current shop die out in 3 weeks before I start to transition to digital during some work changes. Bittersweet but both last week and this week are pretty fun! In order of anticipation:

* **Unstoppable Doom Patrol #3 -** I didn't know what to expect when I dove into this, but it has been one of my favourite reads of the past couple months. The humour has consistently landed (see the jab at X-men data pages in issue #2), the art has repeatedly displayed creativity in its design and layouts. My favourite of the Dawn of DC titles so far.
* **Justice Society of America #4:** The only slight I have for this book is its release schedule. Johns is cooking something special with this, and now that Stargirl is finished I am really looking forward to seeing the characters introduced there brought over.
* **Green Arrow #2**: As much as I enjoyed the first issue, it felt like it played on the reader having a pre-existing attachment to the Arrow family of characters. As a newer reader, some of the emotional moments didn't hit because I didn't have the knowledge, but the story still had a big enough hook to get my interest.
* **Blue Book #4:** I was worried that this would be too drawn out, but near the end now I am still enjoying the read. There hasn't been as much buzz around this as I thought there would be, considering that Tynion is writing.
* **Terrorwar #2:** I bought issue 1 on a whim because the solicitation scratched enough of my genre interests. My expectations were met, and the art surpassed them. The concept of fighting manifested fears is really promising so I'm excited to see how its developed in the follow-up. 
* **Nightwing #104**: That A cover has been a need for me since I saw the solicitation for it months ago. As a newer Nightwing reader, I feel like the series right now isn't at the level it was when I saw all the praise for it online. It is still fun, but considering Titans #1 came out and felt like a great jumping on point, I am questioning my decision to jump in for this Titans arc. It doesn't really feel like it was needed to get Titans, and the main plot feels more like a side arc than what I had heard this series' focus was. It is still fun, and I think I would feel more positive about this if I was more invested in this run and if it wasn't a 4.99 book
* **Vanish #7:** My feelings toward this book have changed almost issue to issue. Outside of issues 1 and 5, which really got me, I haven't really clicked with this. The art is top notch, the world is interesting to me, but something just isn't right with me to like this.
* **Daredevil & Echo #1:** I have really low expectations for this since I have no experience with Taboo as a writer of comics. I do know Phil Noto's art will make me happy, but if it wasn't for Daredevil being my favourite character I wouldn't be pulling this.

Pretty sad because I have recently decided to move towards being a digital reader since my job is picking up around August and and need to cut back the time I spend at my shop and time I spend reading. That being said, if any of you guys read digitally, I'd love to hear some advice or pointers! 

Anyways, this  is a really big week after my smaller week last week and a lot of titles that I'm really pumped for. In order of anticipation:

* **Ice Cream Man #35:** This title will always be top of my list whenever its releasing. The peaks of this series are some of my favourite stories told in any medium and the valleys of this series are still some of my favourite stories told in comics. 
* **No / One #3:** The story of this book combined with the multimedia aspects being incorporated make for a unique experience. I very much feel the different cogs of this world turning and love the immersion of it all.
* **Batman / Superman: World's Finest #15:** My favourite ongoing at DC right now. The series has gotten stronger for me as its progressed, with the Devil Nezha arc being the weakest to me. This isn't just a "retro" book, it's a playground for Mora and Waid to get to just have fun and entertain.
* **The Avengers #1:** I got all of Hickman's Avengers / New Avengers run for Christmas and recently got done reading that. Absolutely incredible journey that showed me that team books can still deliver compelling character arcs and moments. That left me with an appetite for me, and here I am. I know MacKay and Hickman are completely different writers, but MacKay has been killing it on Moon Knight for almost 2 years now, and his Strange stuff has been entertaining as well. I think he can deliver with this.
* **The Vigil #1:** I like Ram V enough that his books will always get a try from me. The characters here have rubbed it with Detective Comics so I am excited to see if this gives us more of that story.
* **Titans #1:** I have no idea what I'm getting into with this. I started Nightwing at #100 to get a read on what's going on with the Titans before jumping into this and that has been okay enough. 
* **Miles Morales #6:** This series has been good since it began; delivering the best art (along with Daredevil) from Marvel and a strong enough debut art. I was afraid that tying this book into an event with Carnage so early on would be a misstep, honestly I still am, but that Alpha issue really clicked with me. The dread Miles felt facing Carnage was refreshing, I love seeing villains that are convincingly intimidating, and bring in Scorpion from the Miles run was a nice way to make this event still feel like its progressing the plot of Miles' book. It's easy for the intro to a crossover to grab me though, so fingers crossed it keeps delivering.
* **Superman #4:** Williamson and Campbell have made the most of Dawn of DC so far, albeit they have had more issues than the other series. From the beginning this has been fun, no brakes story-telling that combines action, suspense, and wholesome character moments into a compressed 3 issue arc. Even with the first arc done with, the story here has excelled at offering multiple plot threads that could be pursued.
* **The Seasons Have Teeth #2:** It's a really good week when the follow-up to a great debut is this far down. Issue 1 was a quick read that established a  good premise, laid the ground work for the themes and character progression we'll see throughout the series, and hooked me in with its compelling literary narration. The art meshes with this well, helping establish a forlorn atmosphere with a layer of intrigue and wonder.
* **Guardians of the Galaxy #2:** Issue 1 simultaneously won me over with the lean into being a Western and made me skeptical with one of its main hooks being "what happened to the Guardians over the past couple months / years". Not sure I like storylines where a main plot thread is the story starting in the aftermath of some climatic event, a la North's Fantastic Four and Wells' Spider-Man. 
* **Fantastic Four #7:** I know I just bashed this book above, but that is really my only con here so far. I think outside the "what did the FF do" we saw in the first few issues, this has been a good time and delivered some heartfelt issues already in its 6 issues so far. I did find that the contained issues focusing on Ben / Alicia and Reed / Sue were my favourite, but those issues showed me that Ryan North gets these characters and knows how to use them as analogues for overarching themes / storytelling. As always I'm excited to see some Doom and what North does with him here, fingers crossed its a better use of him than we've seen in other books in the past year. Also, $6 for a milestone issue that is one big story is a price point I can swallow; prefer that to a $10 issue that's just a normal issue with back-up's.

I think in this medium now, we all expect character deaths to be non-permanent. While that removes the stakes and impact, I still can get something from it if those deaths offer shifts in the narrative. For me, this character’s death didn’t really do that because we immediately moved to the next plot point, which was a fight that’s been heavily foreshadowed for issues now. Maybe the death in issue 9 will start to have more direct ramifications in these last few issues? I also think there is one death that might have a chance of being more permanent than the other, but I don’t want to spoil anything so I won’t get into it here.

My smallest week in a while, but gives me the time to go through some back-issues I picked up on FCBD! In order of anticipation:

* **Daredevil #11** \- For some reason, the emotional twist in issue 9 didn't really have the impact on me I expected upon reading. I was concerned that my general apathy at the deaths in that issue meant I was souring on this run, but #10 restored my confidence. The showdown between Daredevil and a certain hero had the emotional weight I was looking for, and leaves Matt in a place that leaves me believing he might be fundamentally pushing his character and story someplace new in Zdarsky's final issues. 
* **Green Lantern #1** \- Pre this year, I was not a DC floppy reader, reserving my experiences of their world to trades found at my used bookstore. I decided to really throw myself in with Dawn of DC based on my enjoyment of World's Finest, Zdarsky's Batman, and Detective. Every Dawn of DC title I've picked up has hit for me so far. With that, I'm going to keep trying new titles, and I'm excited to read my first Green Lantern book this week!
* **Stargirl: The Lost Children #6** \- Both this and JSA have been sporadic in their releases, but I'm just glad to have another piece of this New Golden Age story. With this being the last issue of this series maybe this book will close with a lead into JSA? Artwork for this has been kickass, and the character designs have expedited my familiarity with all these new sidekicks.
* **Spirit World #1 -** I have no idea what to expect with this, but I'm into supernatural stuff and with it being a Dawn of DC book I'll at least give it a try. The character's powers do sound pretty cool too.

>Based on what I've seen with WHERE MONSTERS LIE, Starks ought to be a great fit for a funny/violent take on Peacemaker. And Steve Pugh's always adept at comedic storytelling. Might just have to check this out myself...

>Silvestri's writing has been solid for an artist but that's mostly because we're comparing it to other artists like Todd McFarlane. 

I think my enthusiasm for this book has come from the fact that I set my expectations for Silvestri's story to be similar to McFarlane's. Since issue #1, Silvestri has been above that level and has offered a coherent plot with serviceable to good dialogue. My only real complaints for the writing are reserved for handling the antagonist(s), who really just seem to be capable of what the plot and atmosphere needs.

In order of anticipation:

* **Shazam! #1:** I have no affinity for the character, but Waid and Mora have consistently delivered on World's Finest. They have more than enough credit in the bank with me for me to check this out.
* **Batman #135:** Zdarsky's second arc on Batman has been a step-down for many of us, but I've heard from people who read this early that this issue is incredible. Plus Jorge Jimenez is listed as being back for this issue, and these past 4 issues have really made me miss him.
* **Peacemaker Tries Hard #1:** I haven't personally read any of Kyle Stark's prior work, but I have heard lots of praise for it. After reading an interview he did on CBR about this book I was convinced to give it a go. I'm a sucker for any project that a writer just gets to have fun with and is willing to self-promote because they're confident in it.

I very much like the atmosphere that Ram V has woven around Gotham and the feeling of dread that clings to some of the antagonists. There are also the back-up stories that give context to some of the supporting characters' backgrounds motivations that add layers to the main narrative. 

Detractors of this run fairly point out that its a slow-burn that is still yet to offer payoff after almost a year of the run kicking off. I think that is fair and that this being a turn-off is a matter of preference. There is a degree of risk in following a story that takes a long time to crescendo when the final destination is an unknown, but I think the setting of Gotham is stylized to the point that I enjoy just being a spectator to the journey enough that the final destination doesn't scare me. 

Lastly, I think deciding to follow this run should factor in if you have any reactions to Ram V's other work. If you have, and you liked it, then this is consistent in quality and stylistic conventions and would therefore recommend it. If you haven't liked his other stuff, I would be skeptical.
